Vieraina taloustieteen professori Niku Määttänen ja valtio-opin apulaisprofessori Hanna Wass. Hallitus on käynnistänyt valmistelun sosiaalisen median kieltämiseksi alle 15-vuotiailta, mutta hallituspuolueet ovat erimielisiä sen toteutuksesta. Tuleeko lasten somenkäyttöön puuttua kansallisella lainsäädännöllä? Aiheesta keskustelevat Nuorisoalan tutkimus- ja kehittämisyksikkö Juvenian tutkimuspäällikkö Sari Tuuva-Hongisto ja nuorisolääkäri Silja Kosola.

Sateenkaarevat esiintyjät ovat usein olleet viisuissa voittoisia - mutta on heitä myös paheksuttu. Kansoja yhdistävään rakkauteenkin mahtuu politiikkaa. Jaksossa aiheesta kertovat muun muassa Nemo, Krista Siegfrids, Baby Lasagna, Anna Muurinen, Dora Royale, Dave Goodman, Dean Vuletic ja Katri Norrlin. O: Pia Asikainen

programme.title: Saariston sankarit
programme.desc: Turun poliisissa Vesan ja Mikon työvuorosta tulee hektinen, kun nuori poika keulii mopolla parkkipaikalla ja aggressiivinen mies häiriköi leirintäalueella. He saavat apua Paraisten saaristopartiolta, jotta mies saadaan ulos alueelta, mutta loppujen lopuksi tilanteessa on käytettävä voimakeinoja. Merivartija Andreas kollegoineen puhalluttaa veneilijöitä Maarianhaminan ulkopuolella. Lähestyvä ukkosmyrsky saa heidät palaamaan asemalle, mutta silloin tulee hälytys kahdesta ajelehtivassa veneessä olevasta alaikäisestä pojasta.

programme.title: Lapin luonto (S)

Tämä ainutlaatuinen 30-osainen sarja on Järven tarina -elokuvan tekijöiden uusi teos, joka sisältää paljon ennennäkemätöntä kuvamateriaalia järviemme salaisuuksista kaikkina vuodenaikoina. Sarjaa on kuvattu kolmen vuoden ajan eri puolilla Suomea: Lapista Järvi-Suomen eteläisimpiin osiin asti, lähteissä, puroissa, joissa ja järvissä.

programme.title: Tanskalainen maajussi
programme.desc: Kastanjapuu, orapihlaja, herneet ja rikkaruohot kasvavat hyvin, mutta villaan istutetut mansikat ovat jääneet pieniksi. Frank rakentaa siirrettävän kanihäkin.

programme.title: Kaipuu maalle - kyläkoulusta koti
programme.desc: Ninni ja Rafael lähtevät etsimään sopivaa keittiötä Tukholmasta, ja samalla Ninni sovittelee morsiuspukuja. Ninni löytää kattopaneeleiden alta vanhoja nimilappuja. Rafael puolestaan suhtautuu kriittisesti Ninnin värivalintoihin. Tuotanto: Parad Media, 2022.

programme.title: Taidekeräilijät
programme.desc: Avioituminen kreivin kanssa teki Marikasta linnanrouvan, mutta muutos ei ollut aivan helppo. Kun hän sai luoda skånelaislinnaan veistospuiston, asiat alkoivat edetä.

programme.title: Talot huokuvat historiaa
programme.desc: Björckin perhe on asunut jo viisi vuotta vanhassa talossa Uplannin maakunnassa, lähellä Knivstan taajamaa. Perheen vanhin poika Axel toivoi perheen kokeilevan elämää maalla eläinten kanssa, ja niinpä toive toteutettiin. Talossa on yhä jälkiä menneistä ajoista. Perhe on saanut ihmetellä niin arvoituksellista valokuvaa kuin aarrearkkua. Rakennustutkija Erika Åberg käy puulattian kimppuun, ja sen alle näyttääkin kätkeytyvän salaisuus. Antiikkiesineiden tuntija Rickard Thunér selvittelee tarinaa nimismiehestä, jonka väitetään kavaltaneen rahaa ja lopulta ampuneen itsensä talon kirjastohuoneessa. Tuotanto: SVT, 2020.

programme.title: Pikku Kakkonen
programme.desc: Katsellaan Susannan kanssa Fantti ja keittiölaitteet, Isot koneet, Henrietta, Haitulan matkassa, Tuuri, Pyöräillään sekä Kengulahti.

programme.title: Suomalaisen naiskoripallon tarina – kohti kotikisoja 2027
programme.desc: Avausjaksossa paneudutaan suomalaisen naiskoripallon kiehtoviin alkuvaiheisiin ja ensimmäisiin tähtiin, kuten Hilkka Hakolaan. Nykyiset huiput Awak Kuier ja Elina Aarnisalo palaavat ajassa taaksepäin kokeilemaan 1950-luvun varusteita ja peliolosuhteita, jolloin koripallo oli vielä hyvin erilaista. Jakso esittelee, miten laji nousi tuntemattomuudesta ja kuinka ensimmäiset legendat inspiroivat uusia sukupolvia.

programme.title: Suomalaisen naiskoripallon tarina – kohti kotikisoja 2027
programme.desc: Uusi sukupolvi, etunenässä Elina Aarnisalo, Sara Bejedi ja Awak Kuier, vie suomalaista naiskoripalloa kohti kansainvälisiä kenttiä ja suuria unelmia. Nykyhetken tähdet ovat esikuvia, jotka jatkavat pioneereilta perittyä rohkeutta ja tasa-arvon edistämistä. Mitä seuraavaksi tarvitaan, jotta suomalainen naiskoripallo menestyy vielä laajemmin?

programme.title: Sportliv
programme.desc: Vuonna 2021 Tuukka Taponen teki suomalaista autourheiluhistoriaa voittaessaan 15-vuotiaana ensimmäisenä suomalaisena kartingin maailmanmestaruuden. Mutta se oli vasta ensimmäinen askel kohti lopullista tavoitetta - F1:n maailmanmestari. Kun formulalupaus ajaa toista kauttaan F3:ssa, vuosibudjetti on puolitoista miljoonaa euroa ja tulot pyöreä nolla. Jos kaikki sujuu suunnitellusti, lohjalaisen elämä näyttää ihan toisenlaiselta parin vuoden kuluttua.

programme.title: Poika, tyttö, koira, kissa, hiiri ja juusto (7)
programme.desc: Rouva Kultala järjestää juhlan, jossa paljastetaan hänen virallinen muotokuvansa. Taiteiljaksi valitaan Koira, mutta maalaaminen ei suju, koska sisarukset ovat jatkuvasti taiteellisen vapauden tiellä.

programme.title: Latela
programme.desc: Jännitys nousee, kun taideteokset paljastetaan raadille. Nyt ratkeaa, kumman tallin teos voittaa.

programme.title: Urkujen synty
programme.desc: Helsingin Musiikkitaloon on rakennettu yhdet Euroopan suurimmista konserttisaliuruista. Säveltäjä Kaija Saariahon tekemästä miljoonan euron lahjoituksesta käynnistynyt projekti kesti kuusi vuotta. Kymmenet eri alojen asiantuntijat suunnittelivat huippumodernia instrumenttia, täysin uusin ratkaisuin. Uniikit, soivat fasadipillit toteutettiin 3D-printtauksella. Kuinka yli 9000 pillin urut suunniteltiin, rakennettiin ja saatiin soimaan konserttisalissa? Ohjaus: Riitta Rask. Tuotanto: Production House (2023).

programme.title: Euroviisut: sotaa ja lovee (7)
programme.desc: Euroviisuihin osallistuminen maksaa, mutta vielä kalliimmaksi tulee euroviisuvoitto. Viisusääntöjä on moneen kertaan rukattu, jotta Euroviisut olisivat kaikkien mieleen. Miten käy viisujen, kun maailma kuohuu, riidat kärjistyvät ja melkein kaikesta on tullut poliittista? Jaksossa aihetta pohtivat mm. Martin Österdahl, Nemo, Baby Lasagna, Alon Amir, Dean Vuletic, Windows95man, Anna Muurinen, Kyösti Salokorpi, Marion Rung ja Bashar Murad. O: Pia Asikainen

programme.title: Ammatti: kirjailija: Veijo Meri
programme.desc: Manillaköydestä Mannerheimiin, kasarmeista Kiveen. Veijo Meren (1928 - 2015) käsissä puhe, tarina tai repliikki muuttui kirjallisuudeksi. Mutta tuliko siitä runo, näytelmä vai osa historiateosta?

programme.title: Saariston sankarit
programme.desc: Palomies Stefan kollegoineen saa hälytyksen läheiselle tehtaalle. Turkulaispoliisit Vesa ja Mikko käyvät vakavan keskustelun varomattomasti ajaneen 17-vuotiaan autonkuljettajan kanssa. Ahvenanmaan merivartiosto löytää mereltä hylkysukeltajia. Marko auttaa saaristopartion Liselottea ja Viktoria ottamaan verinäytteen asiakkaalta, jota epäillään ajoneuvon kuljettamisesta huumeiden vaikutuksen alaisena.

programme.title: Lapin luonto (S)
programme.desc: Lapin ruska on kaunis. Mistä se syntyy ja miten eläimet käyttäytyvät syksyn saapuessa? Jaksossa seurataan Tenon lohen ja taimenten kutua ja kuljetaan aina Jäämeren lintusaarille asti, missä sukelletaan vedenalaiseen maailmaan.

programme.title: Norja veden alla
programme.desc: Olen haave toteutuu, kun hän saa sukeltaa ruijanpallasten keskellä. Äiti maa muistuttaa itsestään ikävällä tavalla. Kokemus Norjan Atlantiksesta jää ikuisesti mieleen. Osa 2/8, T: NRK, 2021

programme.title: Tiettömän taipaleen takana
programme.desc: Hillborg Romtveit ja Trygve Vaagen tiesivät Austliin muuttaessaan, etteivät he rikastuisi elämäntavallaan. Heidän omaisuutensa onkin intohimo musiikkiin, tanssiin ja perinnekäsitöihin, sekä iloinen ja tyyni mieli.

programme.title: Tanskalainen maajussi
programme.desc: 18. tuotantokausi, 9/10. Tuulimyllyn siivet ovat poikki, ja Frank tekee uudet pellistä. Apukeittiön lattiaan upotetaan upea myllynkivi. Uusi kanihäkki pääsee viimein käyttöön, ja pian siellä asuukin kokonainen kaniperhe.

programme.title: Kaipuu maalle - kyläkoulusta koti
programme.desc: Talven kylmyys hiipii Ekkullaan, ja joulumieli on kaikkea muuta kuin huipussaan. Ninni sulattaa jäätynyttä maalia talon lämpimimmässä huoneessa, kun taas väsyneestä Rafaelista tuntuu, ettei työ lopu koskaan. Tuotanto: Parad Media, 2022.

programme.title: Taidekeräilijät
programme.desc: Seikkailija Erling Kaggen naparetket ovat takanapäin. Nyt hän löytää uusia haasteita vaikeana pidetystä nykytaiteesta.

programme.title: Talot huokuvat historiaa
programme.desc: Anette asuu kolmen lapsensa kanssa Gotlannissa vanhassa 1700-luvun talossa. Talo oli ollut vuosia tyhjillään, ja muutto sinne edellytti monenlaista remonttia. Kunnostustöitä tehdessään Anette löysi lattialankkujen alta pinkan tunteellisia kirjeitä, joiden lähettäjä on ollut Amerikkaan muuttanut mies. Kotona häntä oli odottanut oma rakas ja tytär. Anette haluaa tietää, keitä he olivat ja kuinka heidän kävi. Saivatko he toisensa? Vastauksia etsiessään antiikkiesineiden tuntija Rickard Thunér törmää yllätyksiin ja käänteisiin. Yhdessä rakennustutkija Erika Åbergin kanssa perhe uusii talon julkisivun käyttämällä perinteistä gotlantilaista kalkkia. Tuotanto: SVT, 2020.

programme.title: Pikku Kakkonen
programme.desc: Katsellaan Elizabethin kanssa Eeti valmis on, Nalle, Hiiritalon Sam ja Julia, Oravametsä, Pippa ja Popi, Perhejuttu sekä Viiru ja Pesonen.

programme.title: Timanttinen keikka
programme.desc: Egotrippi oli Timanttisella keikalla GLivelabissa syyskuussa 2018. Puoliakustinen keikka kertaa yhtyeen vaiheet kahdenkymmenenviiden vuoden ajalta tähän päivään saakka. Ohjelmassa Mikki ja Knipi pohtivat myös sitä, kuinka he eroavat lauluntekijänä toisistaan, ja millaisia vaiheita yhtyeen uraan on kuulunut.

programme.title: 99 valittua - Huippuorkesterin kulisseissa
programme.desc: Elämän vastoinkäymiset ovat vieneet Pasilta soittokunnon. Emma kärsii huijarisyndroomasta. Eevan vauva ei enää ala itkeä heti kun äiti alkaa soittaa. Tuulan pitää löytää uusi solisti sairastuneen tilalle

programme.title: Eränkävijät
programme.desc: Eränkävijöiden kahdeksannella tuotantokaudella päästään nauttimaan upeista maisemista ja tunnelmasta luonnon rauhassa, unohtamatta vauhdikkaita metsästystilanteita. Katsojien suosikit Aki Huhtanen ja Äijä-koira tekevät paluun ruutuun, ja tuttujen eränkävijöiden lisäksi kaudella nähdään tuoreita kasvoja.

programme.title: Hirvi
programme.desc: Hirvi on tuhansien vuosien ajan ollut osa saamelaista elämää - ravinnon, käsityön, myyttien ja henkisyyden lähde. Samalla se kuuluu suurempaan kiertokulkuun, jossa ihminen ja luonto elävät tasapainossa. Ohjelmassa seurataan hirven jälkiä halki historian. Tarinoiden ja jylhien maisemien kautta saamme kuvan hirven, ihmisen ja luonnon vuorovaikutuksesta.

programme.title: Paratiisi (12)
programme.desc: Hilkka ja Luisa jäljittävät murhaajaa. Andrés siirretään sivuun tutkinnan keskiöstä. Aarne on löytää tiensä lempi kala-apajilleen. Pimeys laskeutuu vääjäämättömästi, niin Espanjassa kuin Suomessakin.

programme.title: The U.S. East Coast

programme.title: The Sun - Inferno in the Sky
programme.desc: On July 23rd, 2012, a massive eruption on the sun hurls a colossal cloud of solar matter into space. It’s the most severe sunstorm in 150 years. Fortunately, the Earth is not in the direct path of this solar ejection. But it’s only a matter of time before a violent solar storm hits us. When these clouds of charged matter reach our planet, they can wreak havoc in electrical systems.

programme.title: mareTV: Scotland's Mild West - On The Inner Hebrides
programme.desc: The Inner Hebrides surprise with green hills, fine sandy beaches and a mild climate, at least as far as Scottish conditions allow. This is ensured by the currents of the Gulf Stream, as well as the Scottish archipelago being protected by its sister islands, which belong to the Outer Hebrides. More than half of the almost 80 islands are uninhabited. Loneliness has made the people rather inventive. On Tiree Island, mathematics, history and physics from the mainland arrive in the classroom per mouseclick. Dr Mauvis Gore and Prof. Rupert Ormond cast off from the island of Mull, after setting a course to encounter a basking shark. The cetohinus maximus is the world's second largest fish and the two scientists are absolutely convinced that the waters surrounding the Mull constitute the mating grounds for the basking sharks. A logistical challenge takes place on the Isle of Easdale each September. Then, around 400 people populate the tiny slate island. Donals Mellon Melville organises the World Skimming Championships, a World Cup in jumping stones. This is all about the distance they are thrown and they must only hop above the water twice.

programme.title: Faroe Islands - A Secret Beauty
programme.desc: The Faroe Islands in the North Atlantic, located in the middle of the Gulf Stream between Scotland and Iceland, are an archipelago of eighteen green volcanic islands where a unique culture has developed over the last thousand years. As direct descendants of the Vikings, the Faroese feel committed to their traditions and hold on to customs, without missing out on the advantages of the modern and globalised world - from archaic hunter and shepherd culture to contemporary art. With the highest birth rate in Europe and the lowest social inequality in the world, the just fifty thousand Faroese are a very special people living on one of the last natural paradises in Europe.

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Some risks on these autoroutes have natural causes: Extreme weather, avalanches and landslides. In some areas, the locals even believe that evil spirits kill travelers. But many of the dangers are man-made: robbers or terrorists lie in wait for travelers, and tough labor pressures, social hardship and greedy mass-transit businesses also cause tragic driving accidents around the world. In the 20th century alone, 35 million people died on roads worldwide - plus 1.5 billion injured! With the two-part Death Roads - On the Road at the Limit, phoenix offers a documentary road movie along the world's most dangerous car routes.

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Roads are much more than just gray strips of asphalt that allow us to travel and trade. For centuries they have been lifelines of mankind, full of stories and history - and in certain countries and areas they also hold great dangers, much human suffering and death. Documentary filmmaker Oliver G. Becker ventured onto dangerous roads in New Zealand, Scotland and Australia for phoenix.

programme.title: Moon, The: Our Gateway To The Universe
programme.desc: We are on the verge of a new age of exploration: besides the plans of NASA and other space agencies, over the next years also privately financed teams are going to send unmanned vehicles to the Moon. The goal is to find a cheap and efficient way to travel there on a regular basis, and in the long term to build a permanent human base.

programme.title: mareTV: Capri and the Amalfi Coast - Italy's Ocean Legends
programme.desc: Capri was already in ancient times a place for the rich and beautiful. Today Capri is one of the most famous islands in the world. Millions of tourists visit it. But there are in fact still unknown corners on the island in the Gulf of Naples. Thus, at the very top of Capri, there is a hermit monastery with a view to the Vesuvius.

programme.title: Wild And Wide Awake - From the Mediterranean to the Alps
programme.desc: The first part of the spring journey takes us from the Spanish inland to the rugged Atlantic and to the Mediterranean, through the French Provence, and finally into the Alps. Along the way, flamingos perform their bizarre dancing rituals, wild horses storm through the wetland… While the North is still covered by snow and ice, the South will soon turn into a blooming garden and every creature is enjoying the first signs of the awakening.

programme.title: Legendary Paddle Steamers
programme.desc: Rugged coasts, untouched nature and the rough climate of the Atlantic characterize the landscape on the west coast of Scotland. In the sounds and lochs of the Scottish West, Waverley, the last seaworthy passenger steamship in the world, appears once a year. The side-wheel steamer was built in 1947 to carry out short ferry passages on the Clyde River. Today, Waverley circumnavigates almost all of Great Britain. The impressive ship was sold to the Paddle Steamer Preservation Society in 1974 for the symbolic price of one English pound. Since then, she starts her season off the Western Isles in Scotland every year in May.

programme.title: Legendary Paddle Steamers
programme.desc: Idlewild - Avalon - Belle of Louisville - these three names stand for the last still roadworthy, historic sternwheeler in the USA. In 1914, the ship was built as Idlewild for the West Memphis Packet Company as a passenger ferry. With a draft of only 1.50 m and a robust steel hull, the boat is suitable for almost all navigable rivers of the Mississippi River system. Today, the Belle is the most traveled steamboat in American history. In the course of her eventful life, she has called at 130 places in 19 states.

programme.title: Legendary Paddle Steamers
programme.desc: With a length of more than 1000 kilometers, the Elbe is one of the largest rivers in Europe. The river has shaped landscapes since time immemorial: geologically, economically and culturally. One of the most beautiful sections of the river - in Saxony in southeastern Germany - has been navigated by the Saxon Steamship Company since 1836. One of its most beautiful ships is the Diesbar. Its engine is considered the oldest paddle steamer engine still in use in the world, the ship is the only steamer in the fleet still powered by coal.

programme.title: Italy's Uncharted Islands
programme.desc: Lake Iseo is located on the southern foothills of the Alps. It extends over the provinces of Brescia and Bergamo in the northern mainland of Italy. In the middle of Lake Iseo lies the largest island of the southern European inland waters. Monte Isola, as the island is called after its central mountain lies close to its two neighboring islands, Isola di San Paolo and Isola di Loreto. As early as the 11th century, a monastic association of Benedictines settled here. For many Italians, Lake Iseo is the most beautiful spot in their homeland. It is all the more astonishing how little the influence of tourism is here. Driving is strictly forbidden on the three islands, and only on Monte Isola. Only on Monte Isola there is a regular bus service in the summertime. Thus, the three islands are an oasis of an oasis of tranquility most of the year. The historical buildings and the nature remind of the long tradition in which the Italians have cultivated this retreat. Only every five years in the autumn a big celebration takes place. Then over 200,000 paper flowers decorate the island. The flowers are reminiscent of the time in the Middle Ages when a Roma woman brought her son to the island to be cured from the from the rampant plague. In gratitude, she donated a sea of flowers. The Festa di Santa Croce has been one of the main attractions in northern Italy ever since. The days are radiant with color, it is the only time when it gets crowded in the small streets of the island villages. The next festival was celebrated in September 2021.

programme.title: Italy's Uncharted Islands
programme.desc: Far from the glamour and spotlight of Lampedusa, Pantelleria is one of the best kept secrets among the Italian islands. Located closer to Tunisia than to the Italian mainland, Pantelleria closer to Tunisia than to the Italian mainland, Pantelleria has been nicknamed The Last Island, a title also given by Giosuè Calaciura gave to his 2016 historical novel set on Pantelleria. Pantelleria, that is the island of lava, capers and of the liqueur wine that comes here Zibibbo. An island with an ancient history, where for centuries farmers and fishermen have pursued their craft. their craft. The famous Zibibbo grapes are cultivated here - among other things also on the vineyard that Gerard Depardieu and his wife Carole Bouquet bought to produce traditional liqueur and nutmeg wine themselves and distribute it worldwide. The cuisine of the island is as much Arabic as Italian, couscous with fish is a typical island dish.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The Halsema Highway, situated on the island Luzon, leads right through the Philippine jungle with its frequent fog and heavy rainfalls. Every trip on this so-called road is an adventure and highly dangerous. We accompany a bus driver and a taxi driver on their challenging trip across the mountains.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The Canadian ice roads exist only for a few months in the winter when the ice is thick enough. The only time of the year when goods can be transported up to Northern Manitoba. We accompany the truckers Vlad and Hugh as well as the aboriginal Canadian Scott with his pick-up on their long journey to a village called God’s Lake. A risky trip in icy temperatures, sometimes even below - 60 degrees Celcius. The men are in constant danger of getting stuck and need to forget everything they ever learnt about driving on a highway in order to arrive safely.

programme.title: Predators of a Different Kind - In the World of the Unknown Sharks
programme.desc: With the aid of modern technology, reveal the unknown behaviour of some unusual species of shark: lemon sharks and their white-tip reef counterparts. Our film trip begins on the Bahamas. To be more precise: in the turquoise-blue waters of the Grand Bahama Bank, in an exactly fixed location. In the spring, 70 – 80 pregnant lemon sharks arrive here. This huge shark population was first discovered just a few years ago by shark researcher, Professor Sam Gruber. Many of the females are tired and rest on the seabed. Pregnant tiger sharks swim in the midst of this group. Without any protection whatsoever, our cameramen shoot their footage, surrounded by sharks and succeed in capturing images hitherto unseen. We continue our journey to Gainesville, Florida, to meet Gordon Hubbell, the leading shark denture expert with the world’s largest shark denture collection. He knows everything about the evolutionary history of the lemon sharks, in addition to those of the white-tip reef variety off Cocos Island, Costa Rica. Here, we encounter large schools of fish, unprecedented numbers of stingrays, as well as hammerhead sharks. However, it is the white-tip reek sharks that make the biggest impression. Their performance begins late at night. Marauding, they patrol in large groups through the reefs and hunt everything that moves. Scales and dead prey fish float above the reef – a welcoming change of diet for the ubiquitous barracudas.

programme.title: Treasure of Lima - Buried Exhibition
programme.desc: This is a story about a remote island in the pacific.

programme.title: Eyes Of The Atacama
programme.desc: ALMA – the Atacama Large Millimeter Array – is the ultimate space observation facility. Here, 66 leviathan parabolic antennae trap cosmic rays in the previously unobservable long-wave range. It can only happen in Atacama, far away from civilisation’s pollution of the night sky with artificial light.

programme.title: mareTV: Majorca
programme.desc: Cleaning woman island, concrete castles, Ballermann: Mallorca's image is negatively affected in some respects. The documentary explores the charm of the largest Balearic island beyond the hustle and bustle of tourism and Rambazamba. The real Mallorca is best explored through real Majorcans: Manolo Barahona, TV fishing expert from the local island broadcaster IB3, faces the most difficult task of the year. The Raor is in season, the most expensive fish on the island. Manolo is supposed to get him first in front of the camera and then in the pan. There's only one catch, the little fish with the piranha teeth just doesn't want to be on TV. In the first months of the year Mallorca turns into a sea of almond blossoms. There are around seven million almond trees on the island, once planted to replace dead vines. But now also the almond trees are threatened. The fire bacterium continues to spread, especially on the large plantations. The farmer Biel Torrens wants to save Mallorca's almond trees and fruit with a small organic plantation and gentle harvesting methods. He shakes the almonds from the tree by hand instead of using a mechanical vibrator.

programme.title: The marvellous World of French Rivers
programme.desc: The Gironde is the largest and most powerful tidal current in Europe. When the Gironde flows into the Atlantic, it is 15 kilometers wide and in the rhythm of the tides, it brings the waters from the Pyrenees and the Massif Central into the ocean. This often pushes its waters far out into the Gironde at high tide.This creates a world of its own that has shaped everything uniquely and intensely for tens of thousands of years. The water surface of the river is so large that the evaporation has created its own microclimate, which is stable and, together with the brackish waters, has influenced flora and fauna on the right and left of the bank for a long time.

programme.title: The marvellous World of French Rivers
programme.desc: The Dordogne consists of a visible and an invisible system of flowing water. Caves and basins under the earth's surface store the excess water and return it to the river when it is dry. A perfect management of a precious resource, not invented by humans, but by the complex nature itself. The result is an ever life-giving river.

programme.title: Myths of the Congo - Apes and Aliens
programme.desc: The Congo, mighty and deep like no other river - yet still a retreat and a habitat for several of our world's strangest animals. Our closest relatives live deep inside the dense jungles: three of the four giant ape species have made the Congo basin their home. Rich in extraordinary footage, the second episode of Myths of the Congo also presents exciting insights into one of the most mysterious and dangerous regions on earth.

programme.title: Myths of the Congo - Deep and Dangerous
programme.desc: The river that swallows all rivers - this is what the natives call it. In reality, the Congo, when considering its water masses, is the second largest and the deepest river in the world. At its source in the north of Zambia, it starts out as a mere trickle, but on its journey westwards it grows and grows, becoming ever mightier and with it, the animals, too: the shoebill stork hides in the dense papyrus. Metre-long pythons hunt for their prey in trees and huge hippos fight for power and respect in the water. To survive in the Congo, animals have to adapt to extreme conditions. Here, evolution has spawned unique creatures: fish with lungs, wings and those that go hunting on land. The Congo River feeds the second largest rainforest on earth. Here is the home of the forest elephant. Time and again, they are summoned to this one, magic place: the Dzanga Bay. Countless other forest dwellers join them. What makes this place so special?

programme.title: World's Most Dangerous Railway Lines
programme.desc: Over 196 bridges and through 55 tunnels, the Bernina Express fights its way from Switzerland to Italy. Powerful forces of nature make the railyway line a dangerous route over the Grisons Alps to this day. The film accompanies the Bernina Express in winter over the highest rail route across the Alps.

programme.title: World's Most Dangerous Railway Lines
programme.desc: The Pamban Railway crosses the tropical landscape of Tamil Nadu, the former Madras, for around 600 kilometers. Heavy storms and rain showers make the route a challenge for Indian Railways to this day. The film accompanies the Rameswaram Express over the notorious Pamban Bridge, the first bridge across the Indian Ocean.

programme.title: World's Most Dangerous Railway Lines
programme.desc: The Ferrocarril del Sur, one of the highest train routes on earth, runs right through the mountains of Peru. To this day, it is considered a miracle in the world of railways. The rails not only lead to the famous ruined city of Machu Picchu but connect the ancient Inca capital of Cusco with Puno on the shores of Lake Titicaca and the gleaming white city of Arequipa. A train journey with the Andes Explorer through a grandiose landscape and an undeveloped and inaccessible area.

programme.title: The Seychelles - Africa with South Seas ambience
programme.desc: The 115 islands and islets that make up the Seychelles present a breath-taking variety of plants, rare animals and beaches laced with palms. This is where the leg-endary Coco de Mer palm nuts grow with fruits weigh-ing up to 20 kilos and giant wild land turtles nibble away at mangrove fruits to their hearts content. The archipelago was first settled at the end of the 18th cen-tury. Today, a very colourful potpourri of peoples in this dwarf state proves just how peacefully different cultures can live side by side. Three times a week, the steamer MV Espoir completes the trip from the main island of Mahé to Praslin and back. A ship for every-one and practically everything: Used cars, toilet paper, horses, bicycles, furniture - you name it, the Espoir transports goods of all kinds. Coconuts sometimes pose a problem as there are far too many of them. What to do with them? The best place to send them is undoubt-edly Hubert Roumien's Virgin Coconut Oil Laboratory, hidden away in the Mahé jungle. Straw turns into gold at Seaweed Seychelles! There, Benjamin Port Louis collects seaweed and extracts liquid fertiliser from it.

programme.title: Europe's far North - Lofoten and the Arctic Ocean
programme.desc: Lofoten is the rugged archipelago in the Norwegian Arctic Ocean. Whoever arrives here is really at the end. Moskenes is the end of the line, and anyone who wants to go further needs a boat or a plane. The only way to get to the open sea is via the Maelstrom, which is quite dangerous. On the outermost headland, there are only a few ruins left. The last inhabitants are long gone, a supply was hardly possible. But fishermen are on the way, mainly to catch cod. And there is the coastal administration, which takes care of broken sea marks and lighthouses. A visit to one of the luxurious ships of the Hurtig Line is not to be missed. They shuttle off rough coasts on an eleven-day trip between the Russian border and southern Norway. A floating workplace for a wide variety of professions. The island of Andøya is not served by the Hurtiglinie. It lies too far out in the Atlantic. One of the most important observatories in Europe is located here. A young woman, Sandra Blindheim, is the boss. She is responsible for the large laser that delivers important information to scientists around the world. On clear winter nights, there is a wonderful panoramic view of the aurora borealis.

programme.title: The Moor
programme.desc: Moors and peatlands are oases in the cultivated landscape of Central Europe.

programme.title: Meteor Menace
programme.desc: On February 15th, 2013, out of the blue, a meteorite exploded in the earth’s atmosphere above the Russian region of Chelyabinsk. The event is a reminder of the ever-present 'Meteor Menace' and the need to understand more about these missiles from outer space.

programme.title: mareTV: Sardinia - Magical Island in the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Sardinia is the second-largest island in the Mediterranean. The Sardin-ians themselves say it's a continent for itself, a virtual world of its own, full of magic: A beach, gleaming in unreal pink shades, red corals protect against the evil eye and the inhabitants seem to remain forever young. On Sardinia, the owners of luxury yachts adopt sheep, fish have gold in their bellies and a giant mussel supplies the material for legendary sea silk. No one is surprised, that the Madonna goes on a sea cruise once a year.

programme.title: Wild Skagerrak
programme.desc: The strait that connects the North Sea with the Baltic, with depths of over 700 metres, is notorious for its dangerously strong currents. But currents also mean food and therefore nourishment for the large swarms of fish that inhabit the region. The sea grass meadows are comparable with those off the Californian coast. Harbour seals, grey seals and orcas hunt here, as do the rare black mouth cat shark and porpoises. Close by, catfish mate, which in itself is quite spectacular and never caught on film in this way before. Lion's mane jellyfish with nettle threads of up to 30 metres in length make their way through the open sea. Skagerrak's coastal regions are amongst the most beautiful and varied in Europe and boast one of the world's great bird paradises. Oystercatchers, sandwich and arctic terns are more plentiful here than anywhere else in Europe. The infinitely long dune landscape of the Skagerrak, is Denmark's answer to the skerries of the Swedish and Norwegian coasts. Large seal colonies can be found in the isolation of the small, picturesque islands and one can come face to face with the animals. In this rough, yet infinitely beautiful landscape, the many streams and rivers that open out into the Skagerrak, are quite remarkable. We accompany salmon in an equally beautiful river landscape and meet with ospreys and sea eagles and eventually come face to face with a brown bear mother and her little ones.

programme.title: Wild Bavaria
programme.desc: The moon disappears behind the horizon and the stage is set for a new day in the Alps of Berchtesgaden.

programme.title: Wild Bavaria
programme.desc: Mighty and mysterious, King Watzmann sits above Germany's only alpine national park.

programme.title: Survival of the Fittest in the Alps
programme.desc: The documentary shows the survival strategies of various animal species in the high mountains of the Alps in winter. Despite freezing temperatures and limited food supply, chamois, red deer and snow hares manage to survive the cold months. Latest research reveals the amazing abilities the animals have developed to adapt to the extreme conditions and also how climate change is altering the behaviour of the alpine inhabitants.

programme.title: Chasing Quakes
programme.desc: Europe has experienced catastrophic earthquakes – even though the 'old continent' is not the most notorious region on Earth for strong quakes, the danger from below is very real. Autumn 2016 tragedy strikes north-central Italy. A series of four earthquakes cracks a mountain and flattens a historic town.

programme.title: Sri Lanka - Tropics, temples and tea plantations
programme.desc: Sri Lanka stands for colourful diversity in all respects. If it's spirituality or Ayurveda you're looking for, here it is. Adventurers and nature lovers can also satisfy their needs here. No one must travel far to discover exotic worlds on this drop-shaped tropical island. mareTV delves into the day to day lives of the is-landers, some of whom pursue the most unusual pro-fessions: Uditha Lakmaal is a palm tree climber. He harvests the sap of the trees, known as palm wine, by climbing to the top of them. Sri Lankan stilt fishermen now actually have very little to do with fish and func-tion more as models receiving payment from tourists for acting the part. Anulawathie runs a small floating hoop business, offering car inner tubes for adults and tuk-tuk tubes for children. Different varieties of tea can be found on Herman Gunaratnes tea plantation. Just four carefully selected women are allowed to harvest the exclusive white tea grown there. Each tea leaf is cut individually from the bush by gloved hands and with golden scissors.

programme.title: Secrets of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: The contours of the Mediterranean have changed during the course of its history. Near Gibraltar, Africa was once connected to the European continent. When the land bridge at Gibraltar collapsed, the Mediterranean basin filled up again. The Suez Canal is today connected to the Red Sea. This route enables animals to reach the Mediterranean, where they cause problems.

programme.title: Secrets of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Rugged rocks, blue sea and idyllic, sandy beaches - this is the Mediterranean as we know it. But this impression is deceptive: the Mediterranean is under constant change. The continents are moving towards one another. Animals, that have to survive under such extreme conditions, must find a way to escape the dangers. Between deserts and volcanoes, the challenges for the animals are enormous.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: The Grand Canyon is a steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, United States. The Grand Canyon is 277 miles (446 km) long, up to 18 miles (29 km) wide and attains a depth of over a mile (6,093 feet or 1,857 meters). The canyon and adjacent rim are contained within Grand Canyon National Park, the Kaibab National Forest, Grand Canyon–Parashant National Monument, the Hualapai Indian Reservation, the Havasupai Indian Reservation and the Navajo Nation. President Theodore Roosevelt was a major proponent of preservation of the Grand Canyon area and visited it on numerous occasions to hunt and enjoy the scenery.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve is an American national park that protects portions of the Brooks Range in northern Alaska. The park is the northernmost national park in the United States, situated entirely north of the Arctic Circle. The park is the second largest in the US, slightly larger in area than Belgium. Gates of the Arctic was initially designated as a national monument on December 1, 1978, before being redesignated as a national park and preserve upon passage of the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act in 1980. A large part of the park has additional protection as the Gates of the Arctic Wilderness that adjoins the Noatak Wilderness. They form the largest contiguous wilderness in the United States together. Fauna include brown bears, black bears, muskoxen, moose, Dall sheep, timber wolves, wolverines, coyotes, lynxes, marmots, porcupines, river otters, red and Arctic fox species, beavers, snowshoe hares, muskrats, bald eagles, golden eagles, peregrine falcons, ospreys, great horned and northern hawk-owls. More than half a million caribou, including the Central Arctic, Western Arctic, Teshekpuk, and Porcupine herds, migrate through the central Brooks Range twice yearly, traveling north in summer, and south in winter. Caribou are important as a food source to native peoples. The park is the northernmost range limit for the Dall sheep. About 132 brown bears reside in the park and preserve, based on a density of about one bear per 100 square miles.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: Saguaro National Park is an American national park in Pima County, southeastern Arizona. The 92,000-acre (37,000 ha) park consists of two separate areas—the Tucson Mountain District (TMD) about 10 miles west of the city of Tucson and the Rincon Mountain District (RMD) about 10 miles east of the city—that preserve Sonoran Desert landscapes, fauna, and flora, including the giant saguaro cactus.An inventory of medium and large mammals in the park confirmed the presence of 30 species in Saguaro National Park between 1999 and 2008. Of these, 21 were found in the Tucson Mountain District and 29 in the Rincon Mountain District. A partial list of the park's mammals includes cougars, coyotes, bobcats, white-tailed deer, mule deer, javelinas, gray foxes, black-tailed jackrabbits, desert cottontails, ring-tailed cats, white-nosed coatis, ground squirrels, and packrats. One endangered mammal, the lesser long-nosed bat, lives part of the year in the park and part of the year in Mexico.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: It is a road of mountain passes and India’s access to the roof of the world – the Himalayas. This 475-kilometre long route at the northernmost tip of the Indian subcontinent connects the cities of Manali and Leh at the heart of the Ladakh region. The term “highway” applies quite literally, since the route traverses five of the highest drivable mountain passes in the world – among these the Lohtang La at 3,978 metres above sea level, the Lachulung La at 5,059 metres and the Tanglang La at 5,325 metres. Crossing these passes is a challenge for both vehicle and man. The mountain peaks, still snow-capped even in the depths of summer, wide variety of vegetation and the fantastic and craggy landscape turn any journey into a captivating adventure.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The “Adriatic Highway” is one of the most beautiful coastal roads in the world. The “technical masterwork” was built in the 1950s and 60s, at the time of Yugoslavian President Tito. Abounding in curves, the asphalt road stretches from Ankaran in Slovenia to Ulcinj in Montenegro. More than half of the road is in Croatia (659 km) and a quarter in Montenegro (125 km). Shorter segments lead through Slovenia; only nine kilometers are in Bosnia and Herzegovina. For all four countries of the former Yugoslavian Federation, the 1,200-kilometer-long highway remains the main thoroughfare of Adriatic tourism. For many travelers, the highway is the absolute dream road. In dizzying heights, it hugs the steep cliffs lining the Adriatic Sea, winds through coves and bays, gardens and stony fields. Wonderful views of the blue sea, green islands, bizarre cliffs and Mediterranean cities and towns are typical of the highway. But with its numerous curves, the dream road also harbors many dangers.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The air wants to flee the heat, but is too weak. It hovers just above the ground, heavy and weighed down by the oven-like heat. It turns wanly around itself, and tries to cool off by liquefying itself. It vibrates, it oscillates – but there is no escape. This is West Africa in late March. The Harmattan, the hot desert wind of the Sahara, is blowing without respite. It has no pity with the people who live here. Whoever wants to go from one place to another has to travel on roads that hardly deserve this name. They are dusty paths that don’t appear on any map. They are maneuverable only with great effort and for a few months of the year. They are impassable during the rainy season, since they are washed over by the Niger River, one of the mightiest rivers in the world. When it starts to rain, the roads turn into muddy paths. Every journey is a trip into uncertainty.

programme.title: Women Above the Clouds
programme.desc: Aerobatics is the supreme discipline in air sports. Only a few pilots dare to navigate a machine during loops, drops and steep flights because nausea and blackouts due to the strong G-forces can be life-threatening. But flight instructor Jenny Holmenes is not deterred - she wants to prove her skills. Although she is still a beginner, she competes in the Sportsman class at the Norwegian Aerobatic Championships.

programme.title: Women Above the Clouds
programme.desc: Nepal is one of the poorest countries in the world. Young women are often disadvantaged here and quite a few are married off before the age of 18. Helicopter pilot Priya Adhikari lives and works here. The 38-year-old is an exception and the only woman in Nepal who ventures into the extremely dangerous heights of the Himalayas in her helicopter.

programme.title: Italy's Uncharted Islands
programme.desc: The Sulcis Archipelago is located off the south-western coast of Sardinia and is part of the province of of southern Sardinia. The islands of San Pietro, Sant'Antioco and Isola Piana form the archipelago, together with several uninhabited islets and rocks form the archipelago. It belongs to the less known areas in Italy and is little developed for tourism. Nevertheless stars like Tom Cruise and Roberto Cavalli come here to enjoy the peace, seclusion and good food. The islanders are only moderately interested in these visitors, and their down-to-earth attitude has never lost.

programme.title: Italy's Uncharted Islands
programme.desc: The Tuscan Archipelago is a group of islands at the height of Florence. The archipelago stretches from the Ligurian Sea to the Tyrrhenian Sea, north-east of Corsica. The archipelago consists of seven main islands - Giglio, Elba, Gianutri, Capraia, Pianisoa, Gorgona and Montecristo - and other smaller islands and rocks. Not all of them are inhabited. We look at the three most extraordinary islands of the archipelago: Elba, Capraia and the island of Montecristo. The Tuscan Archipelago is one of the most important natural wonders of the world and is protected as Parco Nazionale dell'Arcipelago Toscano. With its 61.474 hectares of protected and 17,694 hectares of protected land area, it is the largest marine protected area in in Europe. Capraia is the third largest island of the archipelago and is located with its small harbor in the channel in front of Corsica. The island is an autonomous municipality with about 300 inhabitants. It is also considered the most maritime island of the archipelago. At the end of the eighties, the penal colony on Capraia was closed was closed and the island opened to tourism.

programme.title: Lobsters - The Knights Of The Deep
programme.desc: The knights of the deep are on the move; almost no part of their bodies is without armor. Like medieval warriors, these fighters are well armed – not with sword and shield, but with scissors and forceps and defensive armor that is covered with spikes and hooks. And even though they are well protected and have an uncanny awareness of their surroundings, many of these proud knights will face a gloomy destiny. Many of them will end upon a plate. Gourmets all over the world are in love with these famous crustaceans: lobsters! For marine biologists lobsters are similarly fascinating: as research objects. We are on their trail in Cape Breton, an island in the northern Atlantic and part of the Canadian province Nova Scotia, where one of the largest populations of lobsters has its home.

programme.title: Countries People Adventures - Iceland Extreme
programme.desc: In southeastern Iceland, Europe's largest glacier, the gigantic Vatnajökull, covers an area of around 9,000 square kilometers. Beneath it lie the world's most active and dangerous volcanoes. This extreme landscape is as dangerous as it is fascinating: glistening white glacier tongues, lagoons covered with icebergs, bizarre green lava mountains, snow-covered volcanic cones, solidified lava flows and imposing waterfalls overwhelm everyone who gets to see them. In 2008, Icelanders declared the glacier and adjacent areas a national park, the largest in Europe. In this documentary, the team meets people who live, work or do research here: a life with the dangers of fire and ice in the overwhelming landscape of Vatnajökull National Park.

programme.title: Tren Atlantico
programme.desc: We travel by train from the westernmost point of mainland Europe up to Portugal's only national park, the Peneda-Gerês, and from lively Porto to the Spanish border in the northeast. The train takes you from the blue sea to the green Douro Valley, from the urban metropolis to the scorching heat of the deserted hinterland.

programme.title: Tren Atlantico
programme.desc: Switzerland or Spain? This question is often asked by those who see pictures from northern Spain for the first time: High mountains, lonely villages, but - this is the crucial difference - also breathtaking Atlantic beaches. The Costa Verde, the green coast, is a piece of Spain that is so different from the general tourist image of the Germans' favorite vacation destination. This area has been spared from mass tourism. We travel by train from Bilbao in the Basque Country to Santander in Cantabria and Asturias.

programme.title: Iceland - On Top of the World
programme.desc: A scenic expedition through majestic volcanoes, seething geysers, powerful waterfalls, threatening fjords and almighty glaciers. Hardly any other country offers such a variety of spectacular forces of nature! We will give you an insight on how it can be that the people of a small, distant island with only a fraction of sunlight in some months are happier than the people in more sun-blessed countries.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Razor's Edge - E212
programme.desc: When police find 24-year-old Patrick Ray with a gunshot to the temple, the scene has all the telltale signs of suicide. But Lt. Joe Kenda's instinct says otherwise.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Everybody Lies - E112
programme.desc: After church, deacon Robert Walton is beaten to death in a public park. The case heats up when Lt. Kenda and his team revisit an old friend with a secret. Did the religious leader have a dark side?

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Last Call for Murder - E101
programme.desc: Five people are shot in a cold-blooded robbery. The suspect sets a fire destroying evidence, leaving Kenda a surveillance photo. An exhaustive search ends in a chilling confrontation.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Eyes Wide Shut - E303
programme.desc: A park ranger discovers the corpse of amateur boxer Corey Edge floating in a shallow creek. Kenda learns the victim had ties to the criminal underworld, and investigates a rogue’s gallery of hustlers.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Secret Life - E116
programme.desc: After Lourdes Riddle is found strangled to death in the trunk of her car, homicide detective Joe Kenda follows the trail through a twisting maze of military and cultural secrets.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Blood Innocence - E302
programme.desc: War hero Carl Taylor is beaten to death in the back of an empty semi truck, for no apparent reason. Lt Joe Kenda notices an unusual pattern in the victim’s head wounds.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Preying on the Innocent - E202
programme.desc: When the son of a prominent politician is murdered in his basement, Lt. Joe Kenda feels pressure from City Hall to solve the case.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Primal Fear - E107
programme.desc: A bloody shooting, steps away from a high school, leaves 14-year-old J.L. Jackson dead. Kenda uncovers a deadly vendetta stemming from a heated lunchroom confrontation.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - I Now Pronounce You Dead - E102
programme.desc: Mother of 3 Dianne Hood is shot to death by a masked gunman on her way home from a Lupus support meeting. Joe Kenda uncovers a sordid web of lust and greed, revealing a killer no one ever expected.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Blood Sisters - E213
programme.desc: The bullet-ridden bodies of two sisters are found in a suburban house thatís littered with mysterious clues. Joe Kenda learns that the two unassuming young mothers shared an explosive secret.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Death Grip - E301
programme.desc: When a speeding truck crashes into a residential building, officers find the lifeless body of Michael Faast behind the wheel. But he didnít die in the wreck ñ he was shot point-blank in the temple.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Poker Face - E305
programme.desc: A group of friends discover the corpse of entrepreneur Jamie Foster hidden under a blanket. Kenda e discovers that Foster’s business put him in close quarters with a host of unsavory characters.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Bad Things Come in Threes - E306
programme.desc: When two young mothers are gunned down behind a crowded bar, Kenda has to first determine who was the intended target and who was collateral damage.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Snitch - E307
programme.desc: When officers respond to a shooting, they discover the body of a young man they know all to well -- police informant Jimmie Stevenson. It's up to Lt. Joe Kenda to dtermine who pulled the trigger

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Magic Bullet - E310
programme.desc: A hard-working father of two is shot in the head just steps from a notorious strip club. The case is stuck in neutral until Kenda uncovers a conspiracy origanized by an unlikely triggerman.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - A Prayer for the Dying - E311
programme.desc: A mother of two is found dead in the most expensive part of Colorado Springs, leaving Lt. Joe Kenda stumped -- until lhe looks into her personal life.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - My First Case - E313
programme.desc: In his first case with the homicide unit, rookie burglary detective Joe Kenda volunteers to work a bloody multi-victim shooting deemed unsolvable by the veterans.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - #1 Suspect - E309
programme.desc: Lt. Joe Kenda must somehow solve a stranger-on-stranger crime with just a composite sketch of the killer and a mysterious bouquet of flowers.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Dead Man Falling - E206
programme.desc: When a family of four is brutally murdered, it sends a shockwave of fear through the town. Police believe they have a spree killer on their hands, until Lt. Joe Kenda discovers a gruesome connection.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Bump in the Night - E312
programme.desc: When a pretty, young pilot is found in bed, bound and with a bullet in her hear, Lt. Joe Kenda must determine if this was a random assault or payback for something that happened in the skies.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - The Spy Who Killed Me - E103
programme.desc: Housewife Elsie Jennes is found dead in the basement of her burning home. Lt Joe Kenda has no leads until Elsieís son, William, turns up in a police station over 50 miles away with a story to tell.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Weapon of Choice - E201
programme.desc: When mother of two Shaundra Murr is run over in front of her house, officers initially suspect a hit and run. Until Lt. Joe Kenda uncovers evidence proving Shaundraís murder was a crime of passion.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - River of Blood - E207
programme.desc: Two hunters discover a blood-drenched car, its owner riddled with buckshot. Lt. Joe Kenda learns the car was reported stolen the day before, he follows its trail to a group of unlikely suspects.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Slaughterhouse Six - E105
programme.desc: Solider and young father Layne Schmidtke is brutally beaten to death by a mob of teenagers. Kenda must reconstruct the chaotic scene through forensic evidence and witness testimonies.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Fate Worse Than Death - E211
programme.desc: At the bottom of a steep ravine, joggers discover a body mutilated beyond recognition. To catch a ruthless maniac, Lt. Joe Kenda must first solve the puzzle of the victimís identity.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Murder in a Bottle - E208
programme.desc: Eric Houston is found stabbed to death in a seedy motel, but the ensuing investigation is stymied by a long list of suspects. Lt. Joe Kenda deploys a groundbreaking new technology to catch the killer.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Bump in the Night - E312

programme.title: Observing Europe - Is migration weaponized in Europe?
programme.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested.The Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure.From Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows?

programme.title: BizTalk | AI-powered travel reshaping global tourism
programme.desc: China’s tourism market has continued to heat up this summer. Behind this boom, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how people travel and is opening up new opportunities for the industry – from personalized itineraries to immersive experiences.In this episode of BizTalk, guests from the World Economic Forum, the World Travel And Tourism Council and Atout France explore how smart technologies can enhance visitor experiences, optimize destination management and unlock new growth opportunities. They also examine what China's emerging AI tourism focus could offer the global tourism industry.

programme.title: Meet China: When Chinese Dynamism Reshapes Landscapes — Boundless Challenges, Infinite Vitality
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode...

programme.title: BizPodcast: Why is the US suddenly stepping in to rescue the yen?
programme.desc: The US and Japan have joined forces to prop up the yen — but can intervention really reverse its slide?What's driving the yen's weakness? Why is Washington stepping in? And what can history tell us about the odds of a lasting turnaround?

programme.title: Follow the Money: Where Climate Capital Is Going
programme.desc: Clean energy investment has surpassed fossil fuel supply investment, signaling a fundamental shift in how markets address climate risk. Capital is accelerating into renewables, electrification, and industrial decarbonization—but how do we ensure these funds drive climate action? CGTN's Guan Xin moderates a panel at the 2026 Summer Davos Forum, bringing together voices from government, business, and international institutions to explore the trends, challenges, and prospects of climate capital allocation. Tune in to find out where climate capital is flowing and explore the opportunities in the green transition.#SummerDavos2026

We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode...

programme.title: Observing Europe-So many UK Prime Ministers, same old problems
programme.desc: Since moving to London, CGTN's Li Jianhua has witnessed the UK cycle through four leaders. In this video, Jianhua reflects on the problems facing each of those prime ministers… and why it's affected how he buys grapes.

programme.title: Observing Europe-Who owns Britain?
programme.desc: One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. In this latest episode of his series Observing...

programme.title: Observing Europe - Is migration weaponized in Europe?
programme.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested.The Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure.From Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows?

programme.title: BizTalk | AI-powered travel reshaping global tourism
programme.desc: China’s tourism market has continued to heat up this summer. Behind this boom, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how people travel and is opening up new opportunities for the industry – from personalized itineraries to immersive experiences.In this episode of BizTalk, guests from the World Economic Forum, the World Travel And Tourism Council and Atout France explore how smart technologies can enhance visitor experiences, optimize destination management and unlock new growth opportunities. They also examine what China's emerging AI tourism focus could offer the global tourism industry.

programme.title: Observing Europe-So many UK Prime Ministers, same old problems
programme.desc: Since moving to London, CGTN's Li Jianhua has witnessed the UK cycle through four leaders. In this video, Jianhua reflects on the problems facing each of those prime ministers… and why it's affected how he buys grapes.

programme.title: Observing Europe-Who owns Britain?
programme.desc: One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. In this latest episode of his series Observing...

programme.title: Observing Europe - Is migration weaponized in Europe?
programme.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested.The Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure.From Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows?

programme.title: BizTalk | AI-powered travel reshaping global tourism
programme.desc: China’s tourism market has continued to heat up this summer. Behind this boom, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how people travel and is opening up new opportunities for the industry – from personalized itineraries to immersive experiences.In this episode of BizTalk, guests from the World Economic Forum, the World Travel And Tourism Council and Atout France explore how smart technologies can enhance visitor experiences, optimize destination management and unlock new growth opportunities. They also examine what China's emerging AI tourism focus could offer the global tourism industry.

programme.title: Meet China: When Chinese Dynamism Reshapes Landscapes — Boundless Challenges, Infinite Vitality
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode...

programme.title: No Power, No AI
programme.desc: Is energy the ultimate bottleneck for artificial intelligence? As compute demand skyrockets, can our power grids keep up? CGTN's Michael Wang moderates a critical panel at the 2026 Summer Davos Forum on the intersection of AI and energy infrastructure. We'll explore how to align capital investment, infrastructure build-out, and policy frameworks; future-proof energy supply systems to strengthen energy security; and build a more inclusive, sustainable AI-powered energy future. Tune in as global leaders tackle the energy challenge powering the next wave of AI.#SummerDavos2026

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 1
programme.desc: Nanjing, an ancient city that served as the capital of six imperial dynasties, stands as a testament to China's long-standing history and rich culture. From its Porcelain Tower - one of the Seven Wonders of the Middle Ages, to its grand city walls and ancient palaces, join us on a voyage across time to experience the echoes of history in Nanjing's storied bricks.

programme.title: Wenzhou
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Wenzhou, southeast China — a city famed for its self-made millionaires. Here he meets the first Chinese shoemaker to expand overseas, and hears the stories of other local entrepreneurs. Along the way, he samples traditional snacks, visits some of China’s oldest lighthouses, and enjoys an evening of Ou Opera. He also learns the craft of papermaking, before heading into the hills to soak in hot springs and wander across ancient covered bridges.

programme.title: Back to the Land: Exploring new life in rural China
programme.desc: When we think of the countryside, what colour comes to mind? The answer lies in Wuxin—Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal and Water—an ancient rhythm that still pulses beneath China’s landscapes.In this programme, we explore how the colours of Wuxing come to life through the traditions of China’s ethnic minority groups. From Lugu Lake’s matrilineal water world and the metal-hued fire of the Yi Torch Festival, to Dali’s earth-driven crafts, Guizhou’s wooden Dong dwellings, and the volcanic winds of Inner Mongolia’s new nomadiclife.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He travels to Shannan, the cradle of Tibetan culture. Nestled in the gentlest valley of the Yarlung Zangbo River, this is where the first Tibetan king rose to power, the first palace in Xizang was built, and many other “firsts” in Xizang’s history began. Tianran visits Yamdrok Lake, one of Xizang’s three sacred lakes, where a paragliding base is taking shape. He then learns the art of Tibetan opera, joins rangers on a mission to track the elusive Tibetan red deer, and ends the day with a rejuvenating soak in a village revitalized by hot spring tourism.

programme.title: Foodwise: Haikou
programme.desc: Welcome to Haikou, also known as the Coconut City! Join Tianran He in experiencing the unique culinary culture and urban character of this tropical paradise. From light and sweet coconut chicken hotpot to refreshing herbal desserts and spicy rice soup - a local favourite, every bite tells the story of the city's laid-back charm and beauty. We'll explore everything from Haikou's winding alleys and mangrove forests, to the culture of its southeast Asian diaspora, so come and discover this magical destination with us.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hainan's Four Famous Dishes
programme.desc: The stunning east coast of Hainan in southeast China, attract numerous visitors to travel. The reason that people tend to visit Hianan not only because of the beautiful beach view but also delicious local cuisine in Hainan. Hainan’s four famous dishes is Chicken, duck, goat and crab. In Wenchang, the ancestral home of many overseas Chinese, people could discover the original version of Hainan Chicken Rice and see how local chickens free range on coconut meat. In Qionghai, seat of the Boao Forum for Asia, you may dine on duck and goat, before feasting on crab in the surfer haven of Wanning.

programme.desc: Nanjing, an ancient city that served as the capital of six imperial dynasties, stands as a testament to China's long-standing history and rich culture. programme.title: Wenzhou
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Wenzhou, southeast China — a city famed for its self-made millionaires. Here he meets the first Chinese shoemaker to expand overseas, and hears the stories of other local entrepreneurs. Along the way, he samples traditional snacks, visits some of China’s oldest lighthouses, and enjoys an evening of Ou Opera. He also learns the craft of papermaking, before heading into the hills to soak in hot springs and wander across ancient covered bridges.

programme.title: Back to the Land: Exploring new life in rural China
programme.desc: When we think of the countryside, what colour comes to mind? The answer lies in Wuxin—Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal and Water—an ancient rhythm that still pulses beneath China’s landscapes.In this programme, we explore how the colours of Wuxing come to life through the traditions of China’s ethnic minority groups. From Lugu Lake’s matrilineal water world and the metal-hued fire of the Yi Torch Festival, to Dali’s earth-driven crafts, Guizhou’s wooden Dong dwellings, and the volcanic winds of Inner Mongolia’s new nomadiclife.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He travels to Shannan, the cradle of Tibetan culture. Nestled in the gentlest valley of the Yarlung Zangbo River, this is where the first Tibetan king rose to power, the first palace in Xizang was built, and many other “firsts” in Xizang’s history began. Tianran visits Yamdrok Lake, one of Xizang’s three sacred lakes, where a paragliding base is taking shape. He then learns the art of Tibetan opera, joins rangers on a mission to track the elusive Tibetan red deer, and ends the day with a rejuvenating soak in a village revitalized by hot spring tourism.

programme.title: Exploring Beijing’s Backyard
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the beautiful scenery of Beijing suburbs which is usually ignored by the public. Through self-driving tour, the representative tourism resources in the north of Beijing: Yanqing, Huairou and Miyun are involved, from the scenic spots, food to accommodation. The contents include Mini Three Gorges Longqing Valley, Unique Water Great Wall: Huanghuacheng and Northern Jiangnan : Gubei Water Town.

programme.title: Foodwise: Xishuangbanna Ep.1
programme.desc: What's not to love about Xishuangbanna? From dazzling night markets to lush bamboo forests, 800-year old tea trees to close encounters with elephants, this tropical city in southwest China has everything, and is where the story of tea begins. Join Foodwise for all the Pu'er tea you can drink and feast on everything from banana flowers to elephant food!

programme.title: Foodwise: Xishuangbanna Ep.2
programme.desc: Come get soaked at the Dai people's New Year celebrations! We'll check out buzzing street markets packed with barbecued meats and spicy fruits, crash a foodie auction, and even take part in a rowdy competition, catching fish with our bare hands in the river. programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.5
programme.desc: In this final episode, Tianran journeys to Nyingchi, known as “Xizang’s Garden.” Here, he experiences the region’s semi-pastoral way of life — feeding yaks, trying his hand at archery, and seeing how tourism is transforming lives in Lulang International Tourist Town. Travelling along National Highway 318, Tianran discovers towering millennia-old cypress trees and rafts through the vast Yani National Wetland Park, before ending the day with a unique spa treatment at a traditional Tibetan hospital.

programme.desc: Though excited to learn that she will be working on Christmas Day, Fran is surprised to hear that Maxwell will be producing a benefit in Washington D.C. Told that the Sheffields will celebrate Christmas one day early, Fran is further disappointed to find that Maxwell farms out all of his gift buying to a personal shopper. So, upon finding that the children don't believe in Santa and that what Grace really wants is to have her father home on Christmas, Fran decides to have a talk with Maxwell -- until Niles points out that he is preparing the staff s Christmas bonuses. Revealing that C.C. will also be joining him in Washington but insisting that their trip will be all business, Maxwell is nonetheless persuaded to do his own shopping for a change. So, when Fran relies on Niles' assessment of her bonus and buys the children some expensive gifts, she discovers that, instead of money, Maxwell bought her a beautiful vase. Faced with having to either take back her gifts or somehow pay the bill, Fran declines Niles' offer of a loan and goes to see Val's Uncle Paulie to pawn the vase. But, when Maxwell mentions it later, Fran guiltily rushes to buy it back and, forced to pay twice what she got, sells her grandmother's watch instead. Receiving a call from Niles with word about Fran and the watch, Maxwell decides to make things right. So, leaving C.C. behind at the airport, he intercepts the family at St. Patrick's Cathedral and finds Fran in a confessional seeking help with her financial difficulties. Finally, after returning the watch and then accidentally sitting on the vase, Maxwell ends up at the hospital being treated for his wounds, while Grace gets her wish and renews her belief in Santa Claus.

programme.title: Mothers and Daughters
programme.desc: Korkealla Manhattanin yläpuolella trendikäs ja onnellinen sinkkutyttö Rigby Gray kurkistelee naapureiden asuntoihin ja elämään. Hän piileskelee turvallisesti kameran pitkän linssin takana eikä tiedä, että hänen elämänsä on muuttumassa lopullisesti.

programme.title: Mrs Henderson Presents
programme.desc: Laura Henderson ostaa vanhan lontoolaisen teatterin ja avaa sen Windmill-nimisenä esityssalina, joka jää historiaan muun muassa täysin alastonrevyyjensä ansiosta.

programme.title: Paluu Yorkshireen
programme.desc: Arthur Morrison (Jim Broadbent) saa tietää, että hänellä on syöpä ja vain muutama viikko aikaa elää. Hänen vanhin poikansa Blake (Oscar-voittaja* Colin Firth) muuttaa Yorkshireen äitinsä luokse, kylään jossa hän syntyi. Kun Arthurin tila heikkenee, Blake puntaroi suhdettaan isäänsä.

programme.title: The Shack
programme.desc: Menestysromaaniin perustuva The Shack vie meidät isän kiehtovalle henkiselle matkalle. Perhetragediasta selviytynyt Mack Phillips vajoaa syvään masennukseen ja alkaa epäillä vakaimpia uskomuksiaan...

programme.title: Night Train to Lisbon
programme.desc: Sveitsiläinen professori Raimund Gregorius hylkää luennot ja tiukan elämän lähteäkseen jännittävälle seikkailulle, joka vie hänet matkalle oman sisimpänsä syvyyksiin.

programme.title: The Almond and the Seahorse
programme.desc: Manteli ja merihevonen on elämänmyönteinen, riipaiseva ja kauniisti lohtua antava selviytymistarina, johon me kaikki voimme samastua. Arkeologi ja arkkitehti ponnistelevat kohti uutta tulevaisuutta traumaattisen vamman jätettyä heidät tuuliajolle ja eroon rakkaistaan.

programme.title: From Time to Time
programme.desc: Kummittava aavetarina, joka kattaa kaksi maailmaa, yli vuosisadan erolla. Kun 13-vuotias Tolly saa selville, että hän voi salaperäisesti matkustaa näiden kahden välillä, hän aloittaa seikkailun, joka paljastaa sukupolvien ajan haudatut perheen salaisuudet.

programme.title: Griffin And Phoenix
programme.desc: Kun Griffin saa kuulla, että hänellä on kuolemaan johtava sairaus, hän päättää ottaa kohtalonsa omiin käsiinsä ja elää täysillä loppuun asti. Hän tapaa Phoenixin ja aikaa myöten rakastuu tähän, mutta myös Phoenixilla on salaisuus...

programme.title: Mrs Henderson Presents
programme.desc: Laura Henderson ostaa vanhan lontoolaisen teatterin ja avaa sen Windmill-nimisenä esityssalina, joka jää historiaan muun muassa täysin alastonrevyyjensä ansiosta.

programme.title: Frontera
programme.desc: Arizonan autiomaassa surmataan nainen, ja paikallinen poliisi tyytyy helppoon ratkaisuun syyttäen rikoksesta nuorta meksikolaista pakolaista. Mutta kun naisen leski - entinen seriffi - pääsee salaliiton jäljille, asiat kääntyvät yllättävään suuntaan.

programme.title: The Architect
programme.desc: Arkkitehti Leo Watersin avioliitto säröilee. Hänen vaimonsa Julia ei ole onnellinen, ja heidän poikansa Martin jättää opiskelut kesken ja palaa kotiinsa eksyneenä, eikä oikein onnistu löytämään yhteistä säveltä Leon kanssa.

programme.title: The Samaritan
programme.desc: Vankilatuomion voi istua, mutta menneisyyttä ei voi paeta! Istuttuaan 20 vuotta telkien takana pikkurikollinen nimeltä Foley saa viimein tilaisuuden aloittaa puhtaalta pöydältä.

programme.title: On Wings of Eagles
programme.desc: Eric Liddell on ehkä voittanut kultaa Yhdistyneelle kuningaskunnalle ja hänellä on sointuva ylämaan murre, mutta hän syntyi Kiinassa ja eli siellä yli puolet elämästään evankelioimalla ja opettamalla.

programme.title: Don't Come Knocking
programme.desc: Cowboy-elokuvien ikääntyvä tähti häipyy kuvauspaikalta ja menee tapaamaan äitiään, jota hän ei ole nähnyt 30 vuoteen. Yllätyksekseen hän kuuleekin, että hänellä on lapsi.

programme.title: The Almond and the Seahorse
programme.desc: Manteli ja merihevonen on elämänmyönteinen, riipaiseva ja kauniisti lohtua antava selviytymistarina, johon me kaikki voimme samastua. Arkeologi ja arkkitehti ponnistelevat kohti uutta tulevaisuutta traumaattisen vamman jätettyä heidät tuuliajolle ja eroon rakkaistaan.

programme.title: Viimeinen vuoro
programme.desc: Tom Harper lähtee bussimatkalle Skotlannin pohjoisimmasta kolkasta Englannin etelärannikon Lands Endiin. Bussiaikatauluja, ikäänsä ja kohtaloa uhmaten hän tekee kaikkensa pitääkseen vaimolleen antamansa lupauksen.

programme.title: Sommersby
programme.desc: Vietettyään kuusi vuotta sotavankeudessa sisällissodan aikana ystävällinen etelävaltiolaissotilas palaa tilalleen ja tapaa vaimonsa, joka on luullut hänen kuolleen. Pettynyt kosija paljastaa sotilaan huijariksi, ja että oikeaa Sommersbya syytetään murhasta.

programme.title: Beatrix Potter
programme.desc: Beatrix Potter on 30-vuotias sinkkunainen aikana, jolloin naisen kunnioitettavin tehtävä on mennä hyviin naimisiin. Kukaan, ei edes Beatrixin oma perhe, ymmärrä sitä, että Beatrix haluaa mieluummin piirtää ja kertoa tarinoita eläimistä.

programme.title: American Wrestler: The Wizard
programme.desc: Vuonna 1980 teini-ikäinen poika pakenee Iranin levottomuuksia vain kohdatakseen lisää vihamielisyyksiä Amerikassa panttivankikriisin vuoksi. Päättäväisenä sopeutua hän liittyy koulun horjuvaan painijoukkueeseen.

programme.title: Suffragette
